item.title: Various LLM Smells
item.description:
📝 The LLM generated writing obviously felt significantly better than my own writing. And what is fascinating to me is that ai-smell seems like an artifact that emerges across various AI assisted tasks that you can now easily recognize. LLM writing (beyond the obvious em-dashes):Some picks from my math blog (now deleted) and the drafts that accompanied it Way too many punchlines "Humans trust symmetry because it feels like intelligence made visible.

item.title: Durable Execution the Hard Way
item.description:
📝 Lessons Prerequisites Simple task queue Limiting concurrent tasks Task queue improvements Durable event log Tracking non-determinism Durable tasks Opinions This guide is a somewhat opinionated view on durable execution. item.title: GitHub bans security researcher who posted zero-day Windows exploits
item.description:
📝 In a blog post, Eclipse claims this action was vindictive, stating once again that Microsoft refused communication attempts and that they "got zero pennies from doing so", a likely allusion to unpaid bug bounties from the MSRC program. Eclipse's dramatic dispute with Microsoft has been ongoing since early April, when they published the BlueHammer zero-day without warning. Among other statements, Eclipse says "[they were] told personally by [Microsoft] that they will ruin my life and they did", that there's a dead-man switch of some sort, and that they "will make sure [Microsoft's] bones are shattered.
🔗 Read more: https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/microsofts-github-bans-security-researcher-who-posted-zero-day-windows-exploits-because-company-ruined-their-life-expert-claims-action-is-vindictive-and-promises-further-retaliation

item.title: Announcing Rust 1.96
item.description:
📝 RFC3550 proposed a set of replacement range types that implement IntoIterator rather than Iterator, meaning they can also be Copy. These new macros have not been added to the standard prelude, because they would collide with popular third-party crates that provide macros with the same name. This change was previously announced on this blog, and now takes effect in Rust 1.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/05/28/Rust-1.96.0/
